title: After the Buddha, closed
hook: councils, an emperor, an island, a king's questions, a road south

segments.voice: Yesterday: Theravada and the southern road, from India to Sri Lanka and across to Java. Your line: the southern road. Today, this whole stretch of the story closes.

When a teacher dies, the students face a plain question: now what? The Buddha's own last words, in the Pali account, put the work back in their hands. Decay is part of all compound things, he said; keep striving, with care. Then he was gone, and the teaching had no founder in the room. Everything in this part of the path, from the monks gathering to recite to the saffron line in Laos, answers that question. Today, the whole answer.
screen: `NOW WHAT?` → `KEEP STRIVING, WITH CARE.` → `THE WHOLE ANSWER.`

segments.voice: Five pieces. First, the councils. Monks gathered to recite together what the Buddha had taught, so the words were kept by many mouths instead of one memory. Later councils argued over the rules, and the community began to divide into schools. Second, an emperor. Ashoka, after a bloody war, carved edicts in stone about restraint and kindness, and sent messengers out from India. Third, an island. In Sri Lanka, the chronicles say, Ashoka's son Mahinda brought the teaching, and the island's monks went on to write the Pali texts down. Fourth, a king's questions. In the Questions of King Milinda, a Greek-born king asks the monk Nagasena hard things: if there is no lasting self, who is talking to me? Nagasena answers with a chariot. Is the chariot the wheels? The axle? The pole? None of them alone, and yet the word chariot works. The king is satisfied, and the conversation goes on. Fifth, the road south: Myanmar, Thailand, Laos, Cambodia, Java, with monks, traders and kings carrying it from port to port. Put the five together and one thing stands out. The teaching survived by moving. Every time it was recited, written, carved or carried, it reached someone new, and they shaped it too. The whole stretch in a sentence: it traveled. Tomorrow it turns north.
screen: `THE COUNCILS RECITE TOGETHER.` · `AN EMPEROR CARVES IN STONE.` · `AN ISLAND WRITES IT DOWN.` · `A KING ASKS ABOUT A CHARIOT.` · then, large: `IT TRAVELED.`

segments.voice: Pick one piece: the monks reciting together, the emperor's stones, the island, the chariot, or the road south. Tell it to yourself in three plain sentences, as if to a friend who has never heard it. Then let the story go quiet and rest with the breath.
Chariot. Nagasena's answer to the king's question about the self: no single part is it, and yet the word chariot works.
Your line: it traveled. Each telling carried it a little further. That's day eight hundred ninety-nine.

howItsDone: Buddhist communities retell the history of the councils, Ashoka and Mahinda at festivals and in sermons, and in Sri Lanka the arrival of Mahinda is remembered each year at the Poson full moon.

fork.setup: you're the monk Nagasena. the king asks: if there is no lasting self, who is talking to me? what do you do?
options: ask him whether the chariot is its wheels, its axle or its pole.
tell him the question is forbidden.
fork.reveal: Nagasena turns to the king's own chariot: no single part is the chariot, yet the name works. the king is satisfied, and the questions go on.

trapdoor: what you thought: after the Buddha died, the teaching just continued.
what it means: students had to recite it, argue over it, write it down and carry it.
what a scholar hears: councils, Ashoka's edicts, the Sri Lankan chronicles and the Questions of King Milinda are separate sources, each showing a different way the teaching was kept and moved.

chat.says: If there's no lasting self, who's talking to me right now?
options: Nagasena used a chariot: no single part is it, yet the name works for the parts together.
Nagasena told the king the chariot was really just its wheels, and so is the self.
Nagasena refused to answer, and the king went away without being satisfied at all.
chat.meaning: No single part is the chariot, and yet the word works. The king was satisfied, and the conversation went on.
